artboards.title: Sort & filters — same in all three

annotations.text:
ACTION PLAN — status, priority, created date, sort & filter

Three options for the one decision that changes the build: what the status control on a card IS.

Everything else is identical across the three — the priority picker, the created date, and the sort/filter row at the bottom of this canvas. Pick a row-1 option; rows 2 and 3 follow it.

Drawn from the real app: theme.ts tokens, Newsreader + Hanken Grotesk, 12px radii, the live card anatomy. Content is the three steps from your screenshots.

OPTION A · Segmented bar  (this is what is built and pushed)

All three states visible, one tap to any of them. Current state carries three cues — tint, bold colour, and the underline — so it survives colour-blindness and a dim phone screen.

COSTS: ~46pt of height on every card, and the focus view shows up to 5 cards. Dismiss is not on the card at all (swipe, or the detail screen).

BEST IF: parents move steps backwards as well as forwards, and you want the plan to read as a status board.

OPTION B · Start / Done buttons

The two things a parent actually does, each one tap, each unmistakable. Shortest card of the three. Buttons swap to Done / Back to To Do once a step is started.

COSTS: the current state is implied by which buttons are showing, never stated — you cannot glance at a card and read 'In Progress'. Going backwards is a second-class action.

BEST IF: the plan is a to-do list and forward motion is all that matters.

OPTION C · Big circle + state word

Today's control, made legible: 44pt target, the state spelled out, and a line saying what the next tap does. Smallest change, keeps card density closest to what ships now.

COSTS: still a CYCLE — Done is two taps from To Do, and there is no way to skip In Progress or go straight back. The hint text is doing work the control should do itself.

BEST IF: you want the height back and think most parents only ever tap forward.

THE DETAIL SCREEN (row 2)

Today Status is section 13 of 21 — below the description, the eligibility notes, the documents list and the insider tip. On the screenshot you sent it is not on the page at all.

All three options move it directly under the title, with the priority picker beside it and an 'Added Aug 18' chip in the row below. Dismiss becomes a secondary underlined link rather than a fourth pill sitting one mis-tap from Done.

SORT & FILTERS (row 3) — identical whichever option you pick

Sort: Suggested (today's order) · Due date · Priority · Newest · Oldest. The row scrolls; Filters stays pinned.

Filters sheet: priority, deadline, date added. The count on the button is the receipt that the list is showing a subset.

One behaviour worth agreeing: choosing a sort or a filter turns the next-3 focus view OFF and shows everything that matches. 'Sort by due date' that still shows three of eight, in an order you did not choose, reads as broken.

ONE THING TO DECIDE SEPARATELY

The shipped card draws its status marks as unicode dingbats (○ ◐ ●). Rendering the plan in a headless browser, ◐ fell back to a wrong glyph — a font gap, which some Android builds will also have.

These mockups draw the three marks as inline SVG instead. Cheap to adopt and it removes the font dependency entirely. Say the word and I will switch the built control over.
